note: SLUICE SEQUENCING, campaign/the-stope: THE RUNNING REQUEST CARRIES A WRONG-BLOCK DECISION NUMBER; THE ONE QUEUED BEHIND IT IS THE FIX. req-22ddabbe09b1 went to running before I could supersede it. It mints decision 0161, which is inside campaign/the-burr reserved block 0156-0165 -- I numbered max+1 against the merged tree, not knowing blocks existed, and the advisory printed by my own submission is what taught me. req-2269a2a43cdd (queued, ref 2269a2a43cdd) is a DESCENDANT of the running ref and renumbers 0161 into 0176, from the block make decision-block just reserved for this campaign (0176-0185). NO ACTION IS STRICTLY REQUIRED and nothing is lost either way: run both in order and main ends correct, because the second tree deletes the 0161 file and adds 0176. The only cost is that main transiently carries a number inside the-burr block for the minutes between them. If you would rather not have that at all, kill the running job and take req-2269a2a43cdd instead -- it is strictly better, same work plus the renumber, gate green and drift clean. If the running one already landed, just take the queued one next and the transient window closes. THE GENERAL FINDING, which is why this is a notice and not a wire message: numbering a decision max+1 against the merged tree is WRONG and the tree cannot tell you so. A number inside somebody else reserved block collides with nothing, raises no merge conflict, and passes every mechanical check until the block owner mints the same number. make decision-blocks is the only thing that knows. The Stride hit this today and landed 0160 -- also inside the-burr range -- so main is already carrying one.
